Big Question
Today’s Wonder

The Land God Forgot
Robert W. Service (1907) · from “The Land God Forgot,” stanza 4
· · ·
O outcast land! O leper land! Let the lone wolf-cry all express The hate insensate of thy hand, Thy heart's abysmal loneliness.
· · ·
outcast: driven away and rejected by everyone · leper land: a land everyone shuns, the way people with leprosy were once shunned · insensate: without feeling or reason · abysmal: bottomless, as deep as an abyss

Claim ABuck wants to lead the team because of pride, not only to survive.

(London, Ch. 3)

(London, Ch. 3)
“And this was Buck’s pride, too.”
(London, Ch. 3)
Claim BBy the end of the chapter, Buck plans his moves instead of rushing in.
“He sprang upon Spitz with a fury which surprised them both · · ·”
(London, Ch. 3)
“but he did it craftily, when François was not around · · ·”
(London, Ch. 3)
“Buck never came near Spitz without snarling and bristling menacingly.”
(London, Ch. 3)
Claim CIn this chapter, the North itself fights the team.
“The Thirty Mile River was wide open.”
(London, Ch. 3)

(London, Ch. 3)

🍎 At the Board with Professor Lovelore
Fragments and run-ons in an evidence paragraph
Professor Lovelore At the board
0:38
An AI-generated character and voice.
Where they hide
the becausethe for examplethe end of the quotation
One · The because
Buck attacks. Because he wants the lead.→Buck attacks because he wants the lead.
Two · The for example
For example, when Buck steps in front of Pike.→For example, when Buck steps in front of Pike, Spitz is hurled backward.
Three · After the quotation
London calls Buck “inexorable” (Ch. 3) this shows he has no mercy.→London calls Buck “inexorable” (Ch. 3). This shows he has no mercy.

An AI-generated character and voice.
Four lenses for your draft, and a word check
  1. Claim. Your first sentence says something someone could argue with, and it supports your position.
  2. Evidence. One exact line, introduced and cited.
  3. So what. Two or three sentences explain how the line proves your claim.
  4. Clauses. Every sentence is complete: no fragment, no run-on.
  5. Week words. At least one of this week’s ten words.
100 to 150 words · one paragraph
